key_insight: An octagonal sandwich-panel core raises the transition frequency by up to 70% and reduces modal density relative to honeycomb cores.
engineering_relevance: Core geometry can delay the onset of shear-influenced flexural motion associated with increased modal density and acoustic radiation.
method: Model a periodic unit cell with mesoscopic 3D finite elements.
Use the wave/finite element method to obtain dispersion characteristics without core homogenisation.
Compare core geometries through transition frequency and modal density.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparisons of cellular cores sharing the same mass-to-stiffness ratio, with the octagonal design achieving up to a 70% transition-frequency increase.
watch_item: The abstract does not report experimental validation or quantify acoustic-radiation reductions.
paper_title: Vibro-acoustic optimisation of sandwich panels using the wave/finite element method
